newsitem.title: SPAIN: Latvia hopes for NATO entry within seven years.
newsitem.headline: Latvia hopes for NATO entry within seven years.

text.p: Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis said on Wednesday he hoped the Baltic states would join NATO within five to seven years and had been promised support from successful candidates Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic.
The Kremlin has said it would consider it a threat to its security if Latvia, Lithuania or Estonia, former Soviet republics with substantial Russian minorities, joined NATO.
Ulmanis was speaking to reporters after meeting the leaders of the three former Soviet bloc states invited to join the Western alliance at a NATO summit in Madrid on Tuesday.
He said Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic had promised to support the Baltic states in their drive for NATO membership.
"I think we will join in the near future, within the next five to seven years," Ulmanis told reporters.
Ulmanis was undeterred by Moscow's opposition to NATO membership for the Baltic states, which were annexed by Stalin in World War Two and won independence only in 1991.
"I have already expressed my opinion on the NATO expansion deal and Mr Primakov has the right to express his," Ulmanis said.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on Tuesday denounced NATO's expansion into former Communist eastern Europe as the worst mistake on the continent since World War Two.
But Ulmanis saw it in a different light.
"I think it would not be an exaggeration to compare the NATO deal with events such as the reunification of Germany and the collapse of the Soviet Union," Ulmanis said.
The Latvian president said the Baltic states would draw on the experience of the Hungarians, Poles and Czechs to further their own chances of joining the North Atlantic alliance.
"The three invited countries left socialism militarily stronger than us and in this field we could receive support and advice," Ulmanis said.
